nodes.name: App.tsx
nodes.summary: Root React component for the cockpit frontend; a thin wrapper that renders NarrativeCockpit as the entire application.

nodes.name: Header.tsx
nodes.summary: Cockpit header bar showing scheduler mode, arm-mode state, and wall clock, using tone helpers to color-code mode and arm badges from the snapshot.

nodes.name: PriceChip.tsx
nodes.summary: Small chip component rendering the current ComEd price in cents/kWh with its tier (normal/elevated/scarcity) styling and freshness label.

nodes.name: ThermostatRing.tsx
nodes.summary: Self-contained SVG thermostat dial that maps indoor temperature and cool/heat setpoints onto a circular arc with tick marks, using polar-coordinate helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure SVG rendering with local polar/temp-to-fraction math; no imports at all, fully self-contained.

nodes.name: arm_switch.ts
nodes.summary: Canned Snapshot fixture for the Monday 00:00 CT arm-boundary moment: arm A has just flipped to B-active and the controller is establishing baseline state.

nodes.name: controller_down.ts
nodes.summary: Canned Snapshot fixture where the controller has stopped writing hvac.arm_mode, the watchdog heartbeat reports controller_alive=false, and most flow nodes render as missing (B-down).

nodes.name: feed_outage.ts
nodes.summary: Canned Snapshot fixture for a stale PJM RT LMP feed (>3h gap): controller falls back to schedule-only behavior (B-fallback) and the price node renders stale.

nodes.name: fivecp_risk.ts
nodes.summary: Canned Snapshot fixture for an August PJM capacity-risk window: the ComEd-zone 5CP detector fires and the 5CP layer wins arbitration with an 85F shutoff setpoint.

nodes.name: mild_day.ts
nodes.summary: Canned Snapshot fixture for a mild mid-May day (high < 75F) where all overlays are idle, demonstrating the DAY_TYPE_MILD_HIGH_LT_75 rule path and full evaluation tape.

nodes.name: price_spike.ts
nodes.summary: Canned Snapshot fixture for a July ComEd peak-window price spike (53.4 cents/kWh, scarcity tier) where the price-overlay layer wins arbitration with an 82F cool setpoint.

nodes.name: shadow_current.ts
nodes.summary: Canned Snapshot fixture of a shadow-mode tick; doubles as the runtime fallback snapshot NarrativeCockpit shows when the backend is unreachable with no prior successful fetch.

nodes.name: summer_normal.ts
nodes.summary: Canned Snapshot fixture for a typical July afternoon in experiment mode with normal prices, where the schedule layer wins and no overlays fire.

nodes.name: supervisor_clamp.ts
nodes.summary: Canned Snapshot fixture for hypothetical schedule corruption: a malformed 92F schedule proposal wins arbitration and the safety supervisor clamps it to the 86F ceiling, exercising the clamped role_state visual.

nodes.name: freshness.ts
nodes.summary: Per-source staleness thresholds (fresh/warn/stale/missing) keyed by feed cadence, plus classifyFreshness to bucket an age against them; hand-paired with the scheduler's deploy/energy-stack/hvac_scheduler/freshness.py so the operator sees the same actionability the controller does.
nodes.languageNotes: comed.prices fresh window (7 min) intentionally mirrors the controller's downgrade-recency cutoff, so the indicator cycles green-to-warn each 5-min publish cycle without indicating a feed problem.

nodes.name: api.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal API client exposing fetchSnapshot, which GETs the cockpit backend's snapshot endpoint with AbortSignal support and returns the typed Snapshot.

nodes.name: loadFixture.ts
nodes.summary: Registry mapping the nine named scenario fixtures to their Snapshot objects, with loadFixtureFromUrl resolving the ?fixture= URL parameter for fixture-driven demo/dev rendering.

nodes.name: tone.ts
nodes.summary: UI-state helpers: maps arm mode and scheduler mode to display tones, decides whether writes are allowed for a snapshot, extracts winning lanes from a layer, and formats clock/date strings.

nodes.name: main.tsx
nodes.summary: Vite/React bootstrap entry point that imports global CSS and mounts the App component into the DOM root.

nodes.name: NarrativeCockpit.tsx
nodes.summary: Top-level cockpit page: polls the backend snapshot every 5 seconds (or loads a named fixture via ?fixture=), degrades gracefully to the last successful fetch or the shadow_current fallback fixture when the backend is unreachable, and lays out the hero, center, right, and decision-ribbon panels.

nodes.name: DecisionPipeline.tsx
nodes.summary: Bottom-ribbon component rendering the controller's decision pipeline as a row of cells (weather, day type, schedule, price overlay, 5CP, winner, supervisor, action), built from the snapshot's flow nodes by buildCells.

nodes.name: HeroPanel.tsx
nodes.summary: Left hero panel combining the price chip, a responsively sized thermostat ring (ThermostatHero with ResizeObserver), and contextual readout lines (HeroContext) from the snapshot.

nodes.name: WhyThisDecision.tsx
nodes.summary: Right-panel decision explainer that renders the schedule, price-overlay, winner, and supervisor cards plus an action-sent footer, translating the snapshot's flow details and reason codes into an operator-readable narrative of why the controller chose the current setpoint.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Locked snapshot contract for the cockpit: Snapshot, Flow, BaseNodeEnvelope, and per-node details payloads (weather, day type, schedule, price overlay, 5CP, winner, supervisor, action) plus freshness, role-state, and arm-mode enums shared by the entire frontend.
nodes.languageNotes: BaseNodeEnvelope carries an index signature purely to satisfy React Flow v12's Node<TData extends Record<string, unknown>> constraint.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Default-exported root component that renders NarrativeCockpit.

nodes.name: Header
nodes.summary: Header component rendering scheduler-mode and arm-mode badges (colored via modeTone/armTone) and the formatted clock and date from the snapshot timestamp.

nodes.name: PriceChip
nodes.summary: Renders the current price split into whole and tenths digits with tier-based styling and the feed's freshness label.

nodes.name: ThermostatRing
nodes.summary: Draws the SVG thermostat dial: arc track, tick marks, and markers for indoor temperature and cool/heat setpoints positioned via polar-coordinate math over a clamped temperature range.

nodes.name: classifyFreshness
nodes.summary: Buckets a source's data age into fresh/warn/stale/missing against that source's cadence-specific thresholds; unknown sources default to fresh.

nodes.name: fetchSnapshot
nodes.summary: Fetches the backend snapshot endpoint with an AbortSignal, throws on non-OK responses, and returns the parsed Snapshot.

nodes.name: loadFixtureFromUrl
nodes.summary: Reads the ?fixture= URL parameter and returns the matching named Snapshot fixture from the registry, or null when absent/unknown.

nodes.name: armTone
nodes.summary: Maps each ArmModeActual value (A-active, B-active, B-fallback, B-down, off-protocol, outside-window) to a display tone for badge coloring.

nodes.name: modeTone
nodes.summary: Maps the scheduler mode (shadow/experiment/production) to a display tone.

nodes.name: writesAllowed
nodes.summary: Determines from a snapshot whether the controller is currently allowed to write setpoints to the thermostat (vs shadow/dry-run states).

nodes.name: winningLanes
nodes.summary: Derives which decision lanes are currently winning from a flow layer's role states, for highlighting in the pipeline UI.

nodes.name: formatClock
nodes.summary: Formats an ISO timestamp as a locale time-of-day string for the header clock.

nodes.name: formatDate
nodes.summary: Formats an ISO timestamp as a locale date string for the header.

nodes.name: NarrativeCockpit
nodes.summary: Page component that selects its data source (URL fixture vs 5-second usePolling of fetchSnapshot), falls back to the last fetch or shadow_current on backend errors with a warning banner, and composes Header, HeroPanel, DayAtAGlance, ActionLog, WhyThisDecision, DayAheadPanel, and DecisionPipeline.

nodes.name: DecisionPipeline
nodes.summary: Renders the ribbon of pipeline cells produced by buildCells, styling each by role state and freshness.

nodes.name: buildCells
nodes.summary: Transforms the snapshot's flow nodes into display cells for each pipeline stage, formatting setpoints, price, day type, winner, and supervisor decision values into short labels.

nodes.name: HeroPanel
nodes.summary: Composes the hero column: PriceChip on top, then ThermostatHero and HeroContext.

nodes.name: ThermostatHero
nodes.summary: Responsively sizes the ThermostatRing via a ResizeObserver on its container and renders the large indoor-temperature readout split into whole and tenths digits.

nodes.name: HeroContext
nodes.summary: Renders contextual readout lines under the ring (humidity, setpoints, HVAC/fan mode, weather context) from the snapshot.

nodes.name: WhyThisDecision
nodes.summary: Panel component composing ScheduleCard, PriceOverlayCard, WinnerCard, SupervisorCard, and ActionSentFooter from the snapshot's flow details.

nodes.name: ActionSentFooter
nodes.summary: Footer summarizing the action node: whether a setpoint command fired this tick, its applied/dry-run status, setpoint value, fire timestamp, and last-fire info when idle.

nodes.name: ScheduleCard
nodes.summary: Card explaining the schedule layer: base vs effective cool setpoint, humid override, and precool window details.

nodes.name: PriceOverlayCard
nodes.summary: Card explaining the price-overlay layer: current price, tier transition (held/upgraded/downgraded/released), reason code, and hold minutes remaining.

nodes.name: WinnerCard
nodes.summary: Card showing which layer (schedule or price_overlay) won arbitration, the resulting effective cool setpoint, and whether it changed from the previous tick.

nodes.name: SupervisorCard
nodes.summary: Card showing the safety supervisor's decision (approved/clamped/emergency), the proposed vs final setpoints, and its reason.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: Production entrypoint (`python -m hvac_scheduler.controller`) that wires the rev 4 controller: loads YAML config, builds the Influx price source, the TCC climate adapter, and Influx telemetry, then hands them to ControllerLoop.run_forever.
nodes.languageNotes: Dependency injection at the composition root: every seam (price source, climate, telemetry) is constructed here and passed into the pure loop.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Reads env (SCHEDULER_MODE, TEMP_SCALE, Influx creds, TCC creds), validates config via load_config, constructs the InfluxDB client, TCC adapter, and telemetry, and starts the controller loop; exits non-zero on ConfigError.

nodes.name: InfluxPriceSource
nodes.summary: Thin adapter satisfying the loop's price_source seam: latest(now_utc) delegates to pricing.fetch_price against the live InfluxDB query API.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Rev 4 controller config loader: every tunable is required (no code defaults), temps must sit on the temp_scale grid (0.5 C / 1.0 F), temp_scale must match the TEMP_SCALE env, and config_id is the sha256 of the file bytes for telemetry provenance.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately fails closed: any missing key, off-grid temperature, or invariant violation raises ConfigError instead of falling back to a default.

nodes.name: ControllerConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding the full experimental surface: tier thresholds (elevated_at, scarcity_at), hysteresis, offsets, heat floor, humidity gate bounds, hold TTL, release confirmations, and config_id.

nodes.name: load_config
nodes.summary: Parses the controller YAML, enforces required keys, grid alignment, env/scale coherence, and cross-field invariants (threshold ordering, RH gate ordering), then returns a ControllerConfig stamped with the file's sha256 config_id.

nodes.name: device.py
nodes.summary: Device facade over the whitelisted TCCClimate seam: exposes a synchronous snapshot/push/release interface to the controller loop with one network refresh per snapshot.

nodes.name: ControlSnapshot
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass carrying one device reading: schedule cool, current setpoints, hold state, hold-until slot, indoor temp, and humidity — the data contract the hold logic decides against.

nodes.name: TccClimateAdapter
nodes.summary: Adapts the injected TCC client to the loop's climate seam: snapshot() refreshes and maps device state into ControlSnapshot, push() writes setpoints plus a timed hold-until, release() clears the hold back to the onboard schedule.

nodes.name: holds.py
nodes.summary: Pure hold math for the rev 4 controller (no I/O): warm-only target computation with the engage/extend precondition, quarter-hour hold-until flooring, and the decide() lifecycle that respects manual holds and cleans up expired own holds.
nodes.languageNotes: snap/own parameters are typed Any by design so this module stays pure logic with no imports from device or persistence layers.

nodes.name: compute_target
nodes.summary: Computes the warm-only cool target for a tier (schedule + elevated offset, or the scarcity absolute capped at the ceiling); returns None when the program already sits at or above what the tier would command.

nodes.name: hold_until_minutes
nodes.summary: Converts now-local plus the hold TTL into the thermostat's minutes-past-midnight slot, floored to the quarter-hour grid the TCC NextPeriod encoding requires.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Core hold-lifecycle decision: given tier, device snapshot, own-hold record, and humidity gate, returns push/release/no-op — engaging or extending timed warm holds, deferring to warmer manual holds, actively releasing on normal tier, and zombie-cleaning expired matching holds.

nodes.name: loop.py
nodes.summary: Rev 4 controller runtime: the ControllerLoop tick fetches price, evaluates the tier machine, snapshots the device, runs holds.decide, applies push/release (production mode only), persists the own-hold record, and emits trace/action/arm-mode/price-overlay telemetry.
nodes.languageNotes: Constructor injection seams (price_source, climate, telemetry) let the acceptance test drive the real loop; shadow mode traces decisions without ever touching the device.

nodes.name: ControllerLoop
nodes.summary: Orchestrates one control tick end-to-end (price -> tier -> snapshot -> humidity gate -> decide -> apply -> telemetry) and run_forever() aligns ticks to 5-minute walls with SIGTERM-aware asyncio shutdown and a /tmp/last_tick_ok health touch.

nodes.name: pricing.py
nodes.summary: Rev 4 price input: fetches the latest 5-minute ComEd RTP bucket from InfluxDB and defines fresh-strict (age <= 720s), calibrated to measured ComEd publish-lag jitter; the display-only 7-min freshness label must not gate control.

nodes.name: PriceSample
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for one RTP observation: price in cents, UTC bucket time, and age in seconds at read time.

nodes.name: is_fresh_strict
nodes.summary: The control-gating freshness predicate: a PriceSample is fresh-strict when its bucket age is at most 720 seconds.

nodes.name: fetch_price
nodes.summary: Runs the Flux query for the latest comed.rtp_5min bucket, normalizes the timestamp to UTC, and returns a PriceSample with computed age, or None when the feed is empty.

nodes.name: tiers.py
nodes.summary: Rev 4 tier machine (normal/elevated/scarcity, no time locks): engages on one fresh-strict bucket, releases only after confirm-count distinct buckets at or below the hysteresis-adjusted threshold, and hard-releases to normal on the stale backstop.

nodes.name: TierState
nodes.summary: Immutable state record for the tier machine: current tier, release confirmation count, last confirming bucket time, and last fresh-sample time for the stale backstop.

nodes.name: evaluate_tier
nodes.summary: Pure transition function: applies the stale backstop, ignores non-fresh samples, escalates immediately on one fresh bucket above threshold, and steps down only after enough distinct confirming buckets below the release threshold, resetting confirmations if price pops back up.

nodes.name: tcc_client.py
nodes.summary: Direct Honeywell Total Connect Comfort adapter backed by aiosomecomfort, filling the ThermostatClient/ClimateDevice seam left by the demolished Control4 client; duplicated verbatim into thermostat_poller. Methods keep the legacy _f suffix but pass values through in the device's configured scale (now Celsius).
nodes.languageNotes: No unit conversion happens here despite the _f method names: values flow through in whatever display unit the device is set to, since setpoints are already config-enforced onto the 0.5 degree C grid.

nodes.name: TCCClimate
nodes.summary: Per-device read/write surface: normalizes aiosomecomfort reads to the existing hvac.thermostat strings (Title-case modes, StatusCool hold-index map, raw_ui_data schedule/hold-until fields) and maps writes to setpoint, fan, and timed hold-until calls.

nodes.name: TCCClient
nodes.summary: Session manager for the TCC cloud: lazy login/discover, device lookup by ID, get_climate with refresh wrapped in call_with_reauth, which re-logins and retries once on auth errors.

nodes.name: test_rev4_config.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the rev 4 config loader: full-field load with config_id, named-key errors, no silent defaults (every tunable required), off-grid Celsius rejection, env/scale mismatch rejection, and cross-field invariants.

nodes.name: test_rev4_holds.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the pure hold math: warm-only targets and preconditions, quarter-hour hold-until flooring, engage without schedule reads, warmward-only respect for manual holds, own-hold extend/release, zombie cleanup, and active release on normal tier.

nodes.name: test_rev4_loop.py
nodes.summary: Tests for the controller loop runtime using injected fakes: normal ticks trace without touching the device, missing feed is a traced no-op, humidity hysteresis gating, shadow mode never writes, stale-record hygiene, arm-mode throttling, and the InfluxTelemetry row contracts.

nodes.name: test_rev4_pricing.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the price input: the 720s fresh-strict boundary, fetch_price returning the latest bucket with computed age via a stubbed query API, and None on an empty feed.

nodes.name: test_rev4_tiers.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the tier machine: engage on one fresh bucket, engage blocked when stale, release requiring two distinct confirming buckets, step-down via confirmations, confirmation reset when price recovers, the 30-minute stale backstop, and hysteresis-band hold.

nodes.name: test_tcc_client.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the TCC adapter with aiosomecomfort fully mocked: read normalization to existing hvac.thermostat strings, StatusCool hold-index mapping, write-method mapping, reauth-on-AuthError retry, and get_climate refreshing inside call_with_reauth.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: FastAPI cockpit backend serving the operator dashboard API: /api/health, /api/snapshot, /api/day-ahead, /api/today-actions, and /api/day-at-a-glance. Switches between canned fixture mode (default) and live mode, where it lazy-imports the influx/loki query modules, gathers query results, and hands them to the pure payload builders.
nodes.languageNotes: I/O lives here and assembly logic lives in pure-function modules; live-mode dependencies (influxdb_client, influx, loki, freshness) are lazy-imported inside handlers so canned mode needs no credentials.

nodes.name: day_ahead.py
nodes.summary: Pure payload builder for the cockpit Day-Ahead and Pre-Cool cards: assembles tomorrow's persisted day-type decision (hvac.decisions, written at 21:00) and the price-aware pre-cool window into the response dict, plus a canned variant for fixture mode.

nodes.name: day_at_a_glance.py
nodes.summary: Pure payload builder for the DayAtAGlance chart: 24 hourly price bars (DA forecast plus realized overlay), past-only indoor temperature and setpoint series, and planned future setpoints for the current day_type via the schedules mirror.

nodes.name: freshness.py
nodes.summary: Staleness classification per source cadence — a hand-paired, byte-identical copy of the canonical hvac_scheduler/freshness.py (drift enforced by the check-freshness-drift CI workflow) so the cockpit shows the operator the same actionability cutoffs the controller uses, e.g. the 7-minute comed.prices fresh threshold.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberate duplication with CI-enforced byte parity instead of a shared package import; any edit must land in both copies in the same PR.

nodes.name: schedules.py
nodes.summary: Static mirror of the scheduler's per-day-type ScheduleAction tables (NORMAL/HOT/MILD/HOT_STREAK_DAY1), existing only so the day_at_a_glance endpoint can draw the planned setpoint line. Read-only for display; the controller reads its own canonical constants in hvac_scheduler/app.py.

nodes.name: snapshot.py
nodes.summary: Snapshot assembler — the contract seam between live Influx/Loki data and the cockpit UI. Builds the Snapshot dict matching the TS Snapshot interface in frontend/src/types.ts, with an 8-node decision flow (weather, day_type, schedule, price_overlay, fivecp, winner, supervisor, action) plus thermostat, price, arm-mode, and feed-health sections; offers canned (fixture) and live (pure-function) assembly modes.
nodes.languageNotes: Shape drift against the paired TS fixture is caught by test_snapshot.py's JSON round-trip comparison rather than shared type generation.

nodes.name: summer_normal.py
nodes.summary: Paired Python copy of the frontend summer_normal.ts fixture — a full canonical Snapshot dict (thermostat, price, arm mode, 8-node flow) that must mirror the TS fixture field-for-field; drift surfaces as a test_snapshot.py round-trip failure. Also serves as the canned-mode response body.

nodes.name: test_live_assembler.py
nodes.summary: Mocked tests for build_snapshot_live: synthetic Influx/Loki inputs exercise layer resolution (schedule vs price-overlay vs 5CP winners), supervisor clamping, controller-down rendering, and the locked vocabulary — no live HTTP involved.

nodes.name: test_snapshot.py
nodes.summary: Contract-gate tests for the snapshot seam: canned snapshot must JSON-round-trip equal to the paired TS fixture, plus freshness bucket classification, locked-shape/vocabulary assertions, FastAPI endpoint smoke via TestClient, and price-overlay freshness semantics that track the price bucket rather than the trace tick.

nodes.name: today_actions.py
nodes.summary: Pure payload builder for the ActionLog component: today's planned ScheduleActions for the current day_type with per-item past/current/future status derived from Central wall-clock time.

nodes.name: health
nodes.summary: GET /api/health liveness ping returning ok plus the active backend mode.

nodes.name: snapshot
nodes.summary: GET /api/snapshot route: returns the canned fixture snapshot or delegates to _live_snapshot depending on COCKPIT_BACKEND_MODE.

nodes.name: day_at_a_glance
nodes.summary: GET /api/day-at-a-glance route: canned or live dispatch for the chart payload.

nodes.name: _live_snapshot
nodes.summary: Live-mode snapshot assembly: lazy-imports Influx/Loki clients, runs the latest-thermostat/arm-mode/price/heartbeat/action/forecast/outdoor queries plus feed health and tick traces, then delegates to build_snapshot_live.

nodes.name: day_ahead
nodes.summary: GET /api/day-ahead route: canned or live dispatch for the Day-Ahead and Pre-Cool cards.

nodes.name: _live_day_ahead
nodes.summary: Live-mode day-ahead assembly: queries tomorrow's persisted day-type decision and pre-cool window from Influx, then delegates to build_day_ahead_live.

nodes.name: today_actions
nodes.summary: GET /api/today-actions route: canned or live dispatch for the ActionLog payload.

nodes.name: _live_today_actions
nodes.summary: Live-mode today-actions assembly: pulls the day_type from the latest Loki tick trace and delegates to build_today_actions_live.

nodes.name: _live_day_at_a_glance
nodes.summary: Live-mode day-at-a-glance assembly: queries thermostat history, hourly realized prices, and DA-LMP forecast over today's Central-time window, fetches the day_type trace from Loki, then delegates to build_day_at_a_glance_live.

nodes.name: _build_feed_health
nodes.summary: Builds the feed-health list by querying each feed's last timestamp from Influx and classifying its age via the shared freshness thresholds.

nodes.name: _HttpxLokiClient
nodes.summary: Minimal Loki HTTP client exposing query_range via httpx, standing in for a heavier Loki SDK in live mode.

nodes.name: build_day_ahead_live
nodes.summary: Assembles the day-ahead payload (generated_at, tomorrow's date, day-type card, pre-cool card) from persisted decision rows; pure function over supplied inputs.

nodes.name: _build_day_type_card
nodes.summary: Maps a persisted hvac.decisions row into the Day-Ahead card dict (day type, forecast high/dewpoint, hot-streak flag, decision timestamps), or a missing-state card when no row exists.

nodes.name: _build_precool_card
nodes.summary: Maps a persisted hvac.precool_window row into the Pre-Cool card dict (window hours and reason), or a no-window state when absent.

nodes.name: build_day_ahead_canned
nodes.summary: Canned-mode day-ahead payload: fabricates a representative decision row at a fixed timestamp and reuses build_day_ahead_live for shape parity.

nodes.name: build_day_at_a_glance_live
nodes.summary: Assembles the DayAtAGlance chart payload: indoor and setpoint history series, planned future setpoints for the day_type, and 24 hourly price bars, all anchored to the Central-time day window.

nodes.name: _hourly_bars
nodes.summary: Merges realized hourly average prices with DA-LMP forecast values into 24 per-hour bars keyed by Central-time hour, preferring realized data where present.

nodes.name: build_day_at_a_glance_canned
nodes.summary: Canned-mode chart payload: synthesizes indoor samples, setpoint history, and hourly bars at a fixed timestamp for fixture-mode rendering.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: Classifies a feed's age in milliseconds into fresh/warn/stale/missing using per-source cadence thresholds (e.g. comed.prices fresh under 7 minutes, matching the controller's downgrade-recency cutoff).

nodes.name: PlannedAction
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for one planned schedule step: hour, minute, label, and cool setpoint in Fahrenheit.

nodes.name: planned_setpoints_for_day
nodes.summary: Returns the mirrored ScheduleAction list for a given day_type (NORMAL/HOT/MILD/HOT_STREAK_DAY1) for cockpit display.

nodes.name: build_snapshot_canned
nodes.summary: Returns a deep copy of the SUMMER_NORMAL fixture dict — the canned-mode snapshot and the contract-gate reference shape.

nodes.name: build_snapshot_live
nodes.summary: Top-level live assembler: takes raw Influx/Loki query results (thermostat, arm mode, price, heartbeat, feed health, tick traces, last action, weather, outdoor) and composes the full Snapshot dict including the 8-node decision flow.

nodes.name: _build_thermostat
nodes.summary: Maps the latest thermostat row into the snapshot thermostat section with freshness classification, falling back to a missing-state stub.

nodes.name: _build_price
nodes.summary: Maps the latest ComEd price row into the snapshot price section with tier and freshness classification.

nodes.name: _build_arm_mode
nodes.summary: Maps the latest hvac.arm_mode row into the snapshot arm-mode section (actual mode, arm, freshness).

nodes.name: _build_weather_node
nodes.summary: Builds the Weather flow node from the day-type trace plus live weather and outdoor readings, including forecast high/dewpoint and a human subtitle.

nodes.name: _build_day_type_node
nodes.summary: Builds the Day Type flow node: winning day type, decision basis, and decision timestamp from the tick trace.

nodes.name: _build_schedule_node
nodes.summary: Builds the Schedule flow node: base and effective setpoints from the layer-resolution trace, with role and status reflecting whether the schedule layer won this tick.

nodes.name: _build_price_overlay_node
nodes.summary: Builds the Price Overlay flow node from the price_overlay_eval trace; its freshness deliberately tracks the price bucket age rather than the trace timestamp so a fresh tick cannot mask stale price data.

nodes.name: _build_fivecp_node
nodes.summary: Builds the 5CP flow node (telemetry-only peak-risk layer): active state and scopes from the layer-resolution trace.

nodes.name: _build_winner_node
nodes.summary: Builds the Winner flow node: which layer won resolution, the effective setpoint, and changed/prev details for the operator narrative.

nodes.name: _build_supervisor_node
nodes.summary: Builds the Supervisor flow node from the supervisor trace: decision (pass/clamped), proposed vs final setpoints, and indoor-temp availability caveats.

nodes.name: _build_action_node
nodes.summary: Builds the Action flow node with event-driven semantics (NOT-FIRED-THIS-TICK / last-fire / APPLIED / SHADOW) rather than staleness, since hvac.actions only writes on change.

nodes.name: _classify_tier
nodes.summary: Maps a price in cents to the locked price-tier vocabulary used across the cockpit.

nodes.name: build_today_actions_live
nodes.summary: Assembles today's ActionLog payload: the day_type's planned ScheduleActions each labeled past/current/future against Central wall-clock time.

nodes.name: build_today_actions_canned
nodes.summary: Canned-mode ActionLog payload: reuses build_today_actions_live with a fixed timestamp and day_type.

nodes.name: TestBuildSnapshotLive
nodes.summary: Scenario tests for build_snapshot_live using synthetic query results: schedule-winning happy path, price-overlay scarcity win, 5CP non-winning, supervisor clamp role change, heartbeat-false controller-down rendering, and locked-vocabulary compliance.

nodes.name: TestCannedSnapshot
nodes.summary: Asserts build_snapshot_canned returns the summer_normal shape as an independent deep copy and is JSON-serializable.

nodes.name: TestFreshnessClassification
nodes.summary: Asserts classify buckets ages into fresh/warn/stale/missing at the per-source thresholds.

nodes.name: TestSnapshotContract
nodes.summary: Locks the snapshot contract: top-level keys, locked vocabularies for scheduler_mode/arm-mode/price tier, the 8-node flow, feed-health entry shape, node envelope shape, and winner/schedule detail fields.

nodes.name: TestFastApiEndpoint
nodes.summary: Smoke-tests the FastAPI app via TestClient: /api/health returns ok and /api/snapshot returns the locked shape as deep-independent responses.

nodes.name: TestPriceOverlayFreshness
nodes.summary: Pins _build_price_overlay_node freshness semantics: classification follows the price bucket age (7-minute fresh band and onward), reports missing when the feed is absent, and ignores the trace tick timestamp and orphan staleness flags.

nodes.name: usePolling.ts
nodes.summary: Generic React polling hook for the cockpit frontend: calls a fetch function immediately and on a fixed interval, aborting any in-flight request between ticks, and exposes data/loading/error/lastFetchedAt state. Callers disable it (enabled=false) when the app is pinned to a fixture via URL param.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic over payload type T; an AbortController is recreated per tick so stale responses never clobber fresh state.

nodes.name: useSize.ts

nodes.name: thermal_observer.py
nodes.summary: Pure-Python gray-box thermal model library that fits the house's first-order thermal response (time constant tau, stage-1/stage-2 cooling rates, solar coupling) from telemetry samples via numpy least squares. Enforces acceptance guardrails: holdout skill score vs persistence, plausible tau bounds, stage-2 cooling stronger than stage-1, and minimum per-stage sample counts.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses for immutable samples/intervals/results; the fit rejects rather than silently degrading when guardrails fail, returning a ThermalFitResult with rejection_reasons.

nodes.name: ThermalSample
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for one telemetry sample: timestamp, indoor/outdoor temperature, solar radiation, HVAC cool/heat duty percentages, cooling setpoint, and a setpoint-changed flag.

nodes.name: ThermalInterval
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for a between-sample interval used as a regression row, with derived properties for indoor temperature drift rate (F/hr) and outdoor-indoor envelope delta.

nodes.name: FitConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of fit hyperparameters and acceptance thresholds: sample spacing, stage duty-cycle cutoffs, minimum sample counts, holdout skill threshold, setpoint mask window, and plausibility bounds for tau and stage-2 cooling rate.

nodes.name: ThermalFitResult
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass carrying the fitted thermal parameters (tau, per-stage cooling rates, solar coupling, intercept), fit diagnostics (train/test RMSE, persistence baseline, skill score), acceptance flag with rejection reasons, and a to_json_dict serializer.

nodes.name: build_intervals
nodes.summary: Converts a time-sorted sample series into clean regression intervals, dropping pairs that span data gaps, HVAC stage transitions, non-finite duty cycles, or the 30-minute mask window after a setpoint change.

nodes.name: fit_thermal_response
nodes.summary: Core fit routine: builds intervals, splits train/holdout, solves the linear thermal model with numpy lstsq, derives tau and stage cooling rates, and accepts or rejects the fit against FitConfig guardrails (skill score, tau bounds, stage-2 plausibility, sample minima).

nodes.name: _design_matrix
nodes.summary: Builds the numpy design matrix for the linear fit: envelope delta, stage-1/stage-2 activity indicators, solar radiation, and an intercept column per interval.

nodes.name: _rejected
nodes.summary: Constructs a rejected ThermalFitResult with null parameters, the given rejection reasons, filter counts, and the observed fit window, so callers always receive a structured result even on failure.

nodes.name: thermal_observer_influx.py
nodes.summary: InfluxDB adapter for the thermal observer: builds the Flux query that joins weather and HVAC measurements onto a common sample grid, and converts the returned rows into ThermalSample objects with setpoint-change detection.
nodes.languageNotes: Flux identifiers are sanitized via a regex allowlist and json.dumps quoting before string interpolation into the query, guarding against Flux injection from config values.

nodes.name: rows_to_samples
nodes.summary: Converts Influx query result rows to ThermalSample objects, skipping rows missing required telemetry fields and flagging samples where the cooling setpoint moved by 0.5F or more since the previous row.

nodes.name: build_query
nodes.summary: Assembles the Flux query that pulls the configured outdoor weather measurement and HVAC telemetry, aggregates both onto the sample-minutes grid, and pivots fields into one row per timestamp.

nodes.name: fit_thermal_observer.py
nodes.summary: Read-only CLI entry point that queries Influx for the recent telemetry window, runs fit_thermal_response, and prints a human-readable fit summary. The former --output-json write path is a deprecated no-op, so operator runs never mutate runtime state.

nodes.name: parse_args
nodes.summary: Defines the CLI arguments: fit window, sample spacing, stage duty thresholds, outdoor measurement/field names (defaulting to ecowitt.weather ch1_temp_f), plus deprecated no-op --output-json and --dry-run flags kept for operator-command compatibility.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the fit run: validates required INFLUX_* env vars, builds and executes the Flux query, converts rows to samples, fits the thermal response with the CLI-configured FitConfig, and prints the summary. Returns a nonzero exit code on missing environment.

nodes.name: test_thermal_observer.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the thermal model core: interval-building filters (stage transitions, setpoint mask, non-finite controls), synthetic-data parameter recovery, and every fit rejection guardrail including holdout skill, missing stage-2, implausible tau, and linear-algebra failure.

nodes.name: make_sample
nodes.summary: Test helper that fabricates a ThermalSample at a 10-minute index with configurable indoor/outdoor temperatures, cooling duty, and solar radiation.

nodes.name: test_build_intervals_drops_stage_transition_and_setpoint_change
nodes.summary: Verifies build_intervals excludes interval pairs that cross an HVAC stage transition or a setpoint change while keeping clean steady-state pairs.

nodes.name: test_build_intervals_masks_thirty_minutes_after_setpoint_change
nodes.summary: Verifies the 30-minute post-setpoint-change mask window removes transient intervals from the regression set.

nodes.name: test_build_intervals_drops_non_finite_hvac_control_samples
nodes.summary: Verifies samples with NaN or infinite HVAC duty-cycle values are excluded from interval construction rather than poisoning the fit.

nodes.name: test_fit_thermal_response_recovers_synthetic_tau_and_cooling_rates
nodes.summary: Round-trip accuracy test: generates synthetic samples from known tau and stage cooling rates, then asserts fit_thermal_response recovers those parameters and accepts the fit.

nodes.name: test_fit_rejects_holdout_skill_below_threshold
nodes.summary: Verifies a fit whose holdout skill score falls below min_skill_score is rejected with the corresponding rejection reason.

nodes.name: test_fit_rejects_when_stage2_is_not_observed_in_training_window
nodes.summary: Verifies the fit is rejected when the training window contains no stage-2 cooling activity, preventing extrapolated stage-2 rates.

nodes.name: test_fit_rejects_when_stage2_cooling_is_less_than_stage1
nodes.summary: Verifies the physical-plausibility guardrail that rejects fits where stage-2 cooling is weaker than stage-1.

nodes.name: test_fit_rejects_implausible_tau
nodes.summary: Verifies fits producing a thermal time constant outside the configured tau_min/tau_max bounds are rejected.

nodes.name: test_fit_drops_non_finite_intervals_before_min_sample_check
nodes.summary: Verifies non-finite intervals are filtered out before the minimum-sample-count check, so contaminated data triggers an insufficient-samples rejection rather than a numerical fit.

nodes.name: test_fit_rejects_linear_algebra_failure
nodes.summary: Monkeypatches numpy lstsq to raise LinAlgError and verifies fit_thermal_response returns a structured rejection instead of propagating the exception.

nodes.name: test_thermal_observer_influx.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the Influx adapter: row-to-ThermalSample conversion, skipping rows with missing required telemetry, 0.5-degree setpoint-change flagging, and Flux query construction using the configured weather and HVAC measurement names.

nodes.name: test_rows_to_samples_converts_query_rows_to_thermal_samples
nodes.summary: Verifies a complete Influx row maps field-for-field onto the expected ThermalSample value.

nodes.name: test_rows_to_samples_skips_rows_missing_required_telemetry
nodes.summary: Verifies rows missing any required telemetry field are skipped while complete rows still convert.

nodes.name: test_rows_to_samples_marks_later_sample_when_setpoint_changes_by_half_degree
nodes.summary: Verifies the setpoint_changed flag is set on the later sample when the cooling setpoint moves by at least 0.5 degrees between rows.

nodes.name: test_build_query_uses_configured_weather_and_hvac_measurements
nodes.summary: Verifies build_query interpolates the configured bucket, window, sample interval, and outdoor measurement/field names into the generated Flux query text.

nodes.name: test_fit_thermal_observer_cli.py
nodes.summary: CLI-level test that runs fit_thermal_observer.main against a fake Influx client with synthetic telemetry, asserting a normal run only reads existing fields and never writes: the fake write API raises on any write and no output file is created.

nodes.name: FakeInfluxClient

nodes.name: ArmPeriod
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing one SCED arm period: index, arm label (A/B), and CT-local start/end bounds.

nodes.name: _build_calendar
nodes.summary: Builds the fixed list of 12 alternating A/B arm periods, each 14 days on Sun to Mon 00:00 CT boundaries starting 2026-06-01.

nodes.name: current_arm_at

nodes.name: HourlyRateInputs

nodes.name: HourMode

nodes.name: check_weather_vector_inputs

nodes.name: check_arm_calendar

nodes.name: exit_code_for_status

nodes.name: comed_parser.py

nodes.name: comed_influx.py
nodes.summary: Serializes a parsed ComEd Bill into InfluxDB line protocol (one bill point plus per-line-item points, timestamped to the service-end date at 23:59 America/Chicago) and writes the points to InfluxDB.

nodes.name: parse_comed_bill.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point (run on Pi-lab against handed-off ComEd PDFs) that parses a bill PDF, prints the extracted summary and line protocol, optionally writes it to InfluxDB, and archives the processed PDF into a processed/ directory.

nodes.name: test_influx.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the InfluxDB line-protocol serializer, covering bill and line-item point emission, null peak-kW handling, and the service-end 23:59 America/Chicago timestamp.

nodes.name: test_parser.py
nodes.summary: Comprehensive unit tests for the ComEd bill parser across hourly and fixed-rate PDF fixtures, covering field extraction, block splitting, line-item parsing, total reconciliation, error paths, and end-to-end PDF parsing.

nodes.name: Bill
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass modeling a fully parsed ComEd bill (account, rate plan, service period, kWh, category totals, and line items) with an effective_rate_per_kwh convenience computation.

nodes.name: LineItem
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass representing a single billed line item (category, label, amount, and optional quantity/unit/rate) extracted from a bill block.

nodes.name: normalize_text
nodes.summary: Cleans raw pypdf-extracted bill text into a stable single-spaced form (collapsing whitespace and fixing PDF extraction artifacts) so downstream regex extraction is deterministic.

nodes.name: parse_service_period
nodes.summary: Extracts the bill's service-from and service-to dates and billed day count from normalized bill text via regex.

nodes.name: parse_rate_plan

nodes.name: parse_kwh

nodes.name: _extract_block

nodes.name: parse_line_items

nodes.name: parse_bill

nodes.name: parse_pdf

nodes.name: bill_to_line_protocol

nodes.name: write_bill
nodes.summary: Public write entry point that serializes a Bill to line protocol and writes the points to InfluxDB via the InfluxDBClient write API.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI driver that parses a ComEd PDF, prints the summary and line protocol, conditionally writes to InfluxDB using env-configured credentials, and moves the processed PDF into a processed/ archive folder.

nodes.name: arm_calendar.py

nodes.name: ArmPeriod
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass describing one experiment arm period: 1-based index, A/B arm letter, and inclusive/exclusive CT-local naive start/end bounds.

nodes.name: telemetry.py

nodes.name: TypedRecord

nodes.name: write_point

nodes.name: test_influx_adapter.py

nodes.name: TestProjectRecord
nodes.summary: Test suite for project_record: verifies complete-record projection, ValueError on None value/time, naive-datetime UTC coercion, and float value coercion.

nodes.name: TestWritePoint
nodes.summary: Test suite for write_point using a monkeypatched fake Point: asserts tags/fields are set, timestamps applied when provided and omitted when absent, and int/float/bool/str field values pass through.

nodes.name: poller.py
nodes.summary: CTK04 thermostat poller entry point: reads Honeywell TCC device state every THERMOSTAT_POLL_INTERVAL seconds through a ThermostatClient seam and writes the hvac.thermostat measurement to InfluxDB. Falls back to an inert fail-loud stub when TCC credentials are absent.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses typing.Protocol (ClimateDevice, ThermostatClient) as a device seam plus an asyncio poll loop with signal-driven graceful shutdown and a /tmp health marker.

nodes.name: tcc_client.py
nodes.summary: Direct Total Connect Comfort thermostat adapter backed by aiosomecomfort, filling the ThermostatClient/ClimateDevice seam that replaced the demolished Control4 client. Normalizes read strings to the existing hvac.thermostat vocabulary and does unit-passthrough setpoint writes on the device's native grid.
nodes.languageNotes: Copied verbatim into both hvac_scheduler and thermostat_poller; wraps aiosomecomfort with a login/reauth-on-SessionTimedOut retry wrapper (call_with_reauth).

nodes.name: test_tcc_client.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the TCC adapter covering read normalization (title-case + hold-status index map), setpoint write mapping onto aiosomecomfort, and the relogin-and-retry behavior of call_with_reauth / get_climate.

nodes.name: test_thermostat_poller.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the poller: asserts the override machinery was removed from Config, and drives one full poll cycle against fake Influx/thermostat clients to verify an hvac.thermostat line-protocol row is written without any override fields.

nodes.name: read_snapshot
nodes.summary: Reads one thermostat state snapshot through the ClimateDevice seam, wrapping each accessor in call_with_reauth so a stale TCC session self-heals, and returns a dict of temp/setpoint/mode/humidity fields.

nodes.name: write_snapshot
nodes.summary: Builds the hvac.thermostat InfluxDB Point from a snapshot dict (tagged by thermostat_id) and writes it, mirroring indoor_temp_f into indoor_temp_f_hires for schema continuity since TCC exposes only whole-unit temperature.

nodes.name: main_async
nodes.summary: Async main loop: constructs the InfluxDB client and either a live TCCClient or the inert StubThermostatClient, installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers, then repeatedly reads and writes a snapshot, touches the health marker, and sleeps until the next interval or stop signal.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding poller runtime configuration (TCC device/creds, poll interval, InfluxDB connection) with a from_env factory that fail-loud-exits on missing required environment variables.

nodes.name: ClimateDevice
nodes.summary: typing.Protocol defining the per-read thermostat accessor surface (temperature, setpoints, hvac/fan/hold mode, humidity) that the poller consumes, decoupling snapshot reads from the concrete TCC implementation.

nodes.name: ThermostatClient
nodes.summary: typing.Protocol defining the device-client seam (get_climate plus the call_with_reauth retry wrapper) that both the live TCCClient and the stub satisfy.

nodes.name: StubThermostatClient
nodes.summary: Inert ThermostatClient implementation used when TCC credentials are absent; raises NotImplementedError on any read so a credential-less deploy stays in the known not-yet-wired state instead of emitting fake data.

nodes.name: TCCClimate
nodes.summary: Wraps an aiosomecomfort device to satisfy the ClimateDevice seam: read accessors normalize mode/state/fan/hold strings to the existing hvac.thermostat vocabulary, and set_* methods pass setpoints and holds straight through to the library on the device's native unit grid.

nodes.name: TCCClient
nodes.summary: Total Connect Comfort session manager: lazily logs in via aiosomecomfort, discovers and pins the target device, exposes get_climate returning a refreshed TCCClimate, and provides call_with_reauth which re-logins and retries once on SessionTimedOut.

nodes.name: test_write_mapping_calls_aiosomecomfort
nodes.summary: Verifies TCCClimate setpoint/fan/hold writes forward to the correct aiosomecomfort device methods (set_setpoint_cool/heat, set_fan_mode, set_hold_cool) and that hold writes never touch the heat side.

nodes.name: test_get_climate_refreshes_inside_reauth
nodes.summary: Asserts get_climate performs its device.refresh inside call_with_reauth, so a SessionTimedOut on the first refresh triggers a relogin and the second device is refreshed and returned.

nodes.name: test_call_with_reauth_relogins_and_retries
nodes.summary: Drives call_with_reauth against a coroutine that fails once with SessionTimedOut, confirming it re-logins and retries so the call ultimately succeeds.

nodes.name: test_poll_cycle_writes_thermostat_row_without_override_fields
nodes.summary: End-to-end poll-cycle test that runs main_async against fake Influx and thermostat clients, then asserts exactly one hvac.thermostat line-protocol row is written and that no override fields leak into the output.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: PJM Data Miner 2 to InfluxDB poller: wakes every 5 minutes, and per-feed cron-style schedules fire fetches of day-ahead/real-time LMPs, load forecasts, instantaneous and metered load, RTO peak forecast, and annual NSPL for the ComEd zone and PJM RTO. Writes normalized points, feed-status rows, and a heartbeat, feeding the HVAC scheduler's price awareness and 5CP telemetry.
nodes.languageNotes: PJM `_ept` timestamp fields are always Eastern Prevailing Time (America/New_York) regardless of the operator-local scheduler tz (Chicago); conflating the two is a 1-hour summer offset bug. ComEd zone codes deliberately differ per feed (pnode_id / forecast_area / zone=CE / area=COMED / zone=COMED).

nodes.name: Schedule
nodes.summary: Cron-like per-feed schedule (hours, minutes, optional weekdays/months/days) whose should_fire decides whether a feed is due at a given local wall-clock time.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Runtime configuration dataclass (PJM API key, poll interval, InfluxDB connection, operator timezone) built from environment variables via from_env, exiting hard if the API key is missing.

nodes.name: PJMClient
nodes.summary: Async aiohttp context-manager client for the PJM Data Miner 2 API that authenticates via the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header and returns parsed JSON items from a feed endpoint.

nodes.name: seconds_to_next_aligned_tick
nodes.summary: Computes seconds until the next wall-clock-aligned tick on a fixed interval grid so the poll loop wakes on clean boundaries (e.g. top of each 5-minute slot).

nodes.name: _parse_ept
nodes.summary: Parses a PJM `_ept` timestamp string and attaches the America/New_York (Eastern Prevailing Time) zone so downstream conversion to UTC is DST-correct.

nodes.name: build_rt_lmp_points
nodes.summary: Transforms raw real-time hourly LMP items into pjm.lmp_rt_hourly InfluxDB points, tagging pnode/zone and carrying the four RT price fields; skips rows with a null or missing total_lmp_rt.

nodes.name: build_da_lmp_points
nodes.summary: Transforms raw day-ahead hourly LMP items into pjm.lmp_da_hourly points with pnode/zone tags and the four DA price fields, converting EPT timestamps to UTC.

nodes.name: build_load_forecast_points
nodes.summary: Builds pjm.load_forecast points tagged with forecast_area and evaluated_at_iso (to distinguish forecast revisions) and computes the horizon_hours between evaluation and target time.

nodes.name: build_inst_load_points
nodes.summary: Builds pjm.inst_load points tagged by area from PJM's approximate instantaneous-load feed, the real-time directional input for the 5CP detector.

nodes.name: build_metered_load_points
nodes.summary: Builds pjm.metered_load points tagged by zone, load_area, and is_verified from PJM's settled metered-load feed that seeds the 5CP season-to-date baseline.

nodes.name: build_peak_forecast_points
nodes.summary: Builds pjm.peak_forecast_rto points from PJM's daily RTO peak-load projection, carrying scheduled capacity, operating reserve, and the projected peak datetime.

nodes.name: build_nspl_points
nodes.summary: Builds pjm.nspl_zonal points from the annual Network Service Peak Load allocation snapshot, tagged by zone and year.

nodes.name: fetch_rt_lmp_for_date
nodes.summary: Fetches settled real-time hourly LMPs for an explicit target date (ComEd pnode, current-revision rows only) and returns built points; the reusable primitive the backfill script replays over a date range.

nodes.name: fetch_rt_lmp_recent
nodes.summary: Fetches recent real-time LMPs over a rolling 7-day EPT window filtered to current revisions, the live poller's daily catch-up for settled prices.

nodes.name: fetch_da_lmp_for_tomorrow
nodes.summary: Fetches day-ahead hourly LMPs for tomorrow's delivery date in EPT, fired at 17:00 CT once the DA market has cleared, providing the next-day price curve.

nodes.name: fetch_load_forecast
nodes.summary: Fetches the 7-day load forecast for forecast_area=COMED and returns built forecast points.

nodes.name: _check_rto_metered_load_rows_per_hour
nodes.summary: Tripwire that logs a warning if the RTO metered-load feed returns more than one row per hour, which would signal PJM switched from aggregate to per-zone rows.

nodes.name: _fetch_metered_load_recent_for_zone
nodes.summary: Shared implementation fetching metered load for a given zone over a 5-day EPT lookback window, running the RTO tripwire when applicable, backing both the ComEd (CE) and RTO metered-load feeds.

nodes.name: _fetch_inst_load_recent_for_area
nodes.summary: Shared implementation fetching instantaneous load for a given area over a 30-minute EPT window, backing both the ComEd and PJM RTO 5-minute inst_load feeds.

nodes.name: fetch_peak_forecast_rto
nodes.summary: Fetches PJM's RTO daily peak-load forecast for today in EPT (cooling-season only) and returns built peak-forecast points.

nodes.name: fetch_annual_nspl
nodes.summary: Fetches the annual zonal Network Service Peak Load allocation for zone=COMED, fired once a year on December 1.

nodes.name: _write_feed_status
nodes.summary: Writes a pjm.feed_status observability row per feed (success flag, points written, error type/message) and swallows its own write errors so status logging never breaks the poll cycle.

nodes.name: poll_once
nodes.summary: Single poll cycle: determines which feeds are due from FEED_SCHEDULE, dispatches each fetcher, writes its points and a feed-status row, touches the health marker, and emits a heartbeat, isolating per-feed failures so one bad feed cannot abort the cycle.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Async entry point: loads Config, opens the InfluxDB write API and PJMClient, installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers, and runs the aligned-tick wake loop calling poll_once until stopped.

nodes.name: backfill_rt_hrl_lmps.py
nodes.summary: One-shot idempotent backfill that replays the live poller's fetch_rt_lmp_for_date across a historical date range (default 2026-01-01 through yesterday) to fill pjm.lmp_rt_hourly, respecting the PJM Non-Member 6-calls/60s ceiling via a 15s inter-date sleep.
nodes.languageNotes: DEFAULT_SLEEP_SECONDS pinned at 15.0 by the rate-limit arithmetic (60/sleep + 2 co-tenant inst_load calls <= 6); an earlier 5.0s default produced 66 HTTP 429 failures. DST-aware day completeness: 23 hours (spring forward) and 25 hours (fall back) both count as complete.

nodes.name: BackfillResult
nodes.summary: Accumulator for backfill outcomes tracking written dates and partial/failed dates, with needs_followup signaling whether a re-run is warranted.

nodes.name: backfill_range
nodes.summary: Core backfill loop: iterates each date in the range, calls fetch_rt_lmp_for_date, writes non-empty results, flags days below the DST-aware complete-hour count, sleeps between calls for rate limiting, and continues past transient fetch errors.

nodes.name: _parse_args
nodes.summary: Builds the CLI argument parser (start/end dates, sleep interval, dry-run) with defaults sourced from the module rate-limit and spec-lock constants.

nodes.name: main_async
nodes.summary: Async entry point wiring Config, PJMClient, and the InfluxDB write API into backfill_range, then reporting the BackfillResult and follow-up status.

nodes.name: test_pjm_dm2_poller.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite (111 tests) pinning the PJM DM2 poller and backfill contract: per-feed schedule windows, EPT-vs-Chicago request windows, ComEd/RTO zone-code constants, point-builder tag/field shapes, DST day-completeness, health-marker/heartbeat/feed-status resilience, and the RTO rows-per-hour tripwire.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Docker build for the cockpit observability service: a node:22-slim stage compiles the Vite frontend, then a python:3.13-slim runtime installs backend deps, copies the built UI, and runs the FastAPI app under uvicorn on port 8765 as a non-root user.
nodes.languageNotes: Two-stage build discards the Node toolchain from the final image; the frontend dist is pulled in via COPY --from=frontend-build. Runs as a dedicated non-root uid 1002 (cockpit) user.

nodes.name: frontend-build
nodes.summary: First build stage (node:22-slim) that installs frontend npm deps with npm ci and produces the production Vite bundle via npm run build; its /build/dist output is copied into the runtime image.

nodes.name: python-runtime
nodes.summary: Final runtime stage (python:3.13-slim) that installs backend requirements, copies the backend package plus the built frontend dist, drops to the non-root cockpit user, and serves backend.app:app via uvicorn on 0.0.0.0:8765.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build-context exclusion list for the cockpit image, keeping node_modules, Python caches, prebuilt frontend/dist, logs, reference material, and local .env out of the build to shrink context and avoid stale artifacts.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Container image for the ComEd RTP price poller service, built on python:3.13-slim, installing requirements and running the poller module as an unprivileged system user (uid 1002).
nodes.languageNotes: Layer-caches dependencies by copying requirements.txt before the full source, and drops root privileges via a dedicated 'poller' system user for runtime hardening.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage Docker build for the Rainforest EAGLE energy poller: installs Python deps on python:3.13-slim, copies the eagle_poller package, drops to a non-root system user, and runs the poller module as its entrypoint.
nodes.languageNotes: Layers requirements install before app copy for cache reuse; runs as an unprivileged uid-1001 'poller' user for least-privilege runtime.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Container image for the Ecowitt weather-station receiver: installs Python deps on python:3.13-slim, runs the app as a non-root system user, exposes port 8088, and health-checks GW1200 push freshness via a /tmp/last_push_ok sentinel.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-stage build; HEALTHCHECK asserts upstream liveness by testing that the gateway push sentinel file was touched within the last 7 minutes (GW1200 pushes every 60s).

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage Docker build for the haven_ingest poller service: installs Python deps on a slim 3.13 base, runs as a dedicated non-root user (havenpoll, uid 1009), and launches the haven_ingest.app module with a freshness-based healthcheck.
nodes.languageNotes: HEALTHCHECK asserts liveness by checking that /tmp/last_poll_ok was touched within the last 7 minutes; the poller writes that marker each cycle, so a stale marker marks the container unhealthy.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage python:3.13-slim build for the hvac_scheduler service (the rev 4.1 spike-only controller); installs pinned requirements, runs as unprivileged system user scheduler (UID 1007), and launches the controller module. A HEALTHCHECK marks the container unhealthy if the 60s scheduler tick file goes stale beyond 5 minutes.
nodes.languageNotes: Drops root via a system useradd before CMD, and uses a filesystem-freshness HEALTHCHECK (find -mmin -5 on /tmp/last_tick_ok) as a liveness proxy for the periodic controller loop.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage python:3.13-slim build for the HVAC scheduler watchdog service; installs pinned Python deps and launches the check module as a non-root distinct service identity.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs as a dedicated non-root user (UID 1008, one above the scheduler) so the watchdog has a distinct service identity from the process it supervises.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage init-container image built on influxdb:2.7 that copies the idempotent apply.sh bootstrap script plus the tasks/ Flux definitions, runs once per compose up to apply InfluxDB state (downsampling tasks), then exits.
nodes.languageNotes: Run-once init-container pattern: reuses the influx CLI already bundled in the influxdb base image, applies state idempotently via ENTRYPOINT, and exits rather than staying resident.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Init-container image built on eclipse-mosquitto:2 that runs once per compose up as root to regenerate the broker's password file from environment variables, then exits. Idempotent bootstrap for MQTT authentication.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-stage build; reuses the broker base image so mosquitto_passwd is already present, and runs USER root so the generated password file can be chowned to the unprivileged 1883:1883 runtime user.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage Docker build for the nws_poller service: installs Python dependencies from requirements.txt, copies the poller code into /app/nws_poller, drops root to a dedicated non-root user, and runs `python -m nws_poller.app`. Defines a HEALTHCHECK that fails if the poller hasn't marked a successful poll in the last 60 minutes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a filesystem freshness check (`find /tmp/last_poll_ok -mmin -60`) as the HEALTHCHECK probe instead of an HTTP endpoint, appropriate for a poller with no server surface; runs as a fixed-UID non-root user (poller, uid 1006) rather than a generic appuser, likely to keep UIDs stable/distinct across the stack's services.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage Docker build for the PJM Data Miner 2 poller service, installing Python deps and running as a non-root user. Exposes a loop-liveness HEALTHCHECK (90-min staleness budget on a per-cycle marker) that deliberately ignores per-feed data freshness, which is tracked separately in Influx pjm.feed_status.
nodes.languageNotes: HEALTHCHECK gates on loop liveness (find -mmin -90 on a touched marker), not feed success, so a PJM API outage does not trigger container restarts.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage Docker build for the refoss_poller service on python:3.13-slim, installing requirements, dropping to a non-root uid 1004 user, and running the refoss_poller.poller module with a freshness-based healthcheck.
nodes.languageNotes: HEALTHCHECK asserts a /tmp/last_poll_ok freshness sentinel (touched every ~30s poll, unhealthy if older than 5 min) rather than probing a port; runs as a dedicated non-root system user.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage Docker build for the telegram_notifier service on python:3.13-slim, running as an unprivileged notifier user and launching the alert loop via `python -m telegram_notifier.app`. A HEALTHCHECK marks the container unhealthy if the 5-minute alert tick heartbeat file is stale beyond 10 minutes.
nodes.languageNotes: Non-root runtime via a fixed-uid system user; liveness modeled with a filesystem-heartbeat HEALTHCHECK (find -mmin -10 on /tmp/last_tick_ok) rather than a network probe, matching the service's cron-style alert loop.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage python:3.13-slim image for the thermostat-poller service; installs requirements, runs as unprivileged UID 1008, and exec's the poller module with a freshness HEALTHCHECK that marks the container unhealthy if /tmp/last_poll_ok is older than 15 minutes.
nodes.languageNotes: Drops to a non-root system user (UID 1008, one above hvac-scheduler) and uses a find-based HEALTHCHECK on a poll-success sentinel file rather than an HTTP probe.

nodes.name: check-freshness-drift.yml
nodes.summary: PR-triggered GitHub Actions workflow that fails the build if the two duplicated freshness.py modules (hvac_scheduler and cockpit/backend) have drifted, comparing them after stripping their header docstrings.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an inline python3 ast parser inside a bash step to strip leading docstrings before diffing, so the canonical/paired files can differ only in their opening docstring.

nodes.name: deploy.yml
nodes.summary: Canonical deploy pipeline: on push to main touching deploy/**, an ubuntu-latest runner joins the tailnet as an ephemeral tag:ci node, rsyncs the energy-stack to Pi-lab over Tailscale SSH, runs docker compose build/up, and smoke-tests that no service crashed.
nodes.languageNotes: Two-job pipeline with change detection (detect job gates deploy-energy-stack via needs/if outputs); Tailscale ephemeral node replaces the decommissioned self-hosted runner; concurrency group serializes deploys instead of cancelling in-flight.

nodes.name: typecheck.yml
nodes.summary: Branch-protection type-check pipeline that installs every in-scope service's requirements plus dev deps under Python 3.13 and runs run_typecheck.sh (mypy) with a cached mypy store.
nodes.languageNotes: Explicitly enumerates each service's requirements.txt (not a glob) to exclude the out-of-scope scripts/ dir; workflow name and job name are both type-check so the branch-protection required-check name is predictable.

nodes.name: config.json
nodes.summary: Understand-Anything plugin configuration: enables incremental auto-update of the knowledge graph on commit and sets English as the output language for generated summaries.

nodes.name: fingerprints.json
nodes.summary: Per-file content fingerprints (423 files) keyed to a git commit, used by the Understand-Anything auto-update hook to detect which sources changed and re-patch only those nodes in the knowledge graph.
nodes.languageNotes: Large machine-generated hash manifest; stamped with gitCommitHash + generatedAt so the auto-update hook can diff against the current tree.

nodes.name: knowledge-graph.json
nodes.summary: Committed Understand-Anything knowledge graph for the project (1064 nodes, 1545 edges, 9 layers, 10-step tour); canonical structural map queried for cross-file dependency, blast-radius, and flow questions per AGENTS.md.
nodes.languageNotes: Machine-generated graph artifact with nodes/edges/layers/tour sections; ~1.1 MB, queried by grep rather than loaded whole.

nodes.name: meta.json
nodes.summary: Analysis run metadata for the Understand-Anything knowledge graph: timestamp, git commit hash, tool version, and the count of analyzed files (424) at last full build.

nodes.name: INDEX.md
nodes.summary: Canonical, hand-curated map of all active documentation in the repo, grouped by intent (entry points, controller logic, telemetry, methodology, ops, tools) and serving as the authoritative starting point for agents and humans.
nodes.languageNotes: Carries a YAML front-matter header (date, owner, status, role-label) per the project's doc-hygiene discipline.

nodes.languageNotes: YAML front-matter header plus shields.io badges and an embedded architecture diagram reference.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Canonical type-checker and import-linter configuration for the monorepo: strict mypy 3.13 settings, per-service test-module relaxations, pydantic-mypy plugin, and forbidden import-linter contracts enforcing the influx_adapter and tcc_client adapter boundaries.

nodes.name: .sops.yaml
nodes.summary: SOPS creation-rules configuration defining the recipient key used to encrypt the stack's secrets backup (secrets/*.sops.env), the recovery path for the Pi-lab-only .env.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Operational guide of record for the energy-stack Docker Compose deployment: services-at-a-glance, authoring/deploy flow over Tailscale, first-time Pi-lab bootstrap, ops cheat sheet, running tests, type checking, ports, secrets handling, and the profile=mqtt ComfortNet pipeline.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Docker Compose definition for the full Pi-lab energy stack: InfluxDB and Grafana, the cockpit dashboard, the ComEd/PJM/Eagle/Refoss/NWS price and energy pollers, the HVAC scheduler and its watchdog, thermostat/Ecowitt/Haven ingest, the Telegram notifier, Loki/Promtail logging, and the Mosquitto/Telegraf MQTT pipeline.

nodes.summary: Shared pytest configuration for all energy-stack services (asyncio_mode=auto), and the documented rationale for why a per-service wrapper is required: each service's top-level app.py collides in sys.modules under pytest's default prepend import mode.

nodes.name: run_tests.sh

nodes.name: run_typecheck.sh

nodes.name: .env.example

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Operator guide for the Controller Cockpit observability dashboard: canonical run as the Pi-lab compose service versus the workstation dev loop, plus architecture, layout, stack, visual-acceptance, and test notes across 10 sections.

nodes.name: install-shortcut.ps1
nodes.summary: One-time setup script that drops 'Cockpit' and 'Stop Cockpit' desktop shortcuts wiring pwsh (ExecutionPolicy Bypass) to start-cockpit.ps1 and stop-cockpit.ps1 for double-click launch of the dev cockpit.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the WScript.Shell COM object to author .lnk shortcuts, a Windows-native pattern.

nodes.name: start-cockpit.ps1

nodes.languageNotes: Targeted process cleanup matches Win32_Process CommandLine against a cockpit pattern so unrelated node/python on those ports are left alone.

nodes.name: stop-cockpit.ps1

nodes.name: Stop-CockpitOnPort
nodes.summary: Finds the process listening on a given port and force-stops it only if its command line matches the cockpit pattern, warning and leaving alone any non-cockpit owner.

nodes.name: Wait-Url
nodes.summary: Polls a URL until it returns a sub-500 status or the timeout elapses, used to wait for the backend health endpoint and the Vite dev server to come up.

nodes.name: Stop-CockpitOnPort
nodes.summary: Finds the process listening on a given port and force-stops it only if its command line matches the cockpit pattern, sparing unrelated processes on that port.

nodes.name: New-LnkShortcut
nodes.summary: Creates a Windows .lnk shortcut targeting pwsh with the given script, arguments, description, and working directory via the WScript.Shell COM object.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: HTML entry document for the Reticule Energy Cockpit SPA; sets dark/ember theme attributes, preloads Google fonts, and mounts the React app by loading /src/main.tsx into the #root div.

nodes.name: package.json

tour.title: What This Project Is
tour.description: Start here to learn the mission: monitor a home's real-time and historical energy use, then shave HVAC cost by reacting to ComEd's 5-minute real-time prices. README.md frames the Arm A (thermostat's own comfort program) vs Arm B (that same program plus price awareness, warm-only drift) design; PROJECT.md gives the phase-by-phase build history and hardware inventory; INDEX.md is the hand-curated map of every active doc, so you always know where to look next.

tour.title: The Binding Controller Design
tour.description: Before reading any controller code, read the contract it implements. This rev 4 spike-only commissioning spec is the source of truth for intent: the thermostat's onboard schedule stays in command, and the controller only pushes timed, warm-only holds through the Honeywell cloud during price spikes. It defines the program spine, the reactive core, feed-gap behavior, device-owned safety, and the temp_scale units every later step assumes.

tour.title: Entry Point & the Tick Loop
tour.description: This is how the controller actually starts. `__main__.py` is the production entrypoint (`python -m hvac_scheduler.controller`): it loads the YAML config, builds the Influx price source, the TCC device adapter, and the telemetry sink, then hands them to ControllerLoop. `loop.py` is the beating heart from Step 2's spec: each tick fetches price, evaluates the tier machine, snapshots the device, runs the hold decision, applies push/release (only in production mode), persists its own-hold record, and emits telemetry. Every following step zooms into one collaborator this loop orchestrates.
tour.languageLesson: In Python, `python -m package.controller` executes the package's `__main__.py` as the program entrypoint — the standard way to make an importable package also directly runnable, keeping wiring (main) separate from logic (loop).

tour.title: Config: The Experimental Surface
tour.description: The spec calls config 'the experimental surface' — baseline, offsets, thresholds, ceiling, and hold TTL all live in YAML, while code owns only invariants. `config.py` enforces those invariants hard: every tunable is required (no silent code defaults), temperatures must land on the temp_scale grid (0.5 C / 1.0 F), the file's temp_scale must match the TEMP_SCALE env, and config_id is the sha256 of the file bytes so every telemetry row can be traced back to the exact config that produced it.

tour.title: The Price Signal
tour.description: This is the controller's only live control input. `pricing.py` fetches the latest 5-minute ComEd RTP bucket from InfluxDB and applies a 'fresh-strict' rule: a price older than 720 seconds is refused, a threshold calibrated to ComEd's measured publish-lag jitter. Note the deliberate split the spec demands — the 7-minute freshness label is display-only and must never gate control. Stale price means the controller stands down rather than acting on bad data.

tour.title: The Tier State Machine
tour.description: Given a fresh price from Step 5, `tiers.py` decides how expensive 'now' is: normal, elevated, or scarcity. Critically it has no time locks — it engages on a single fresh-strict bucket, but releases only after a confirm-count of distinct buckets sit at or below a hysteresis-adjusted threshold, and hard-releases to normal on the stale backstop. This asymmetry (fast to react, slow to relax) is what keeps the controller from flapping between tiers on noisy price data.

tour.title: Warm-Only Holds & Zombie Cleanup
tour.description: The tier from Step 6 becomes an actual setpoint here. `holds.py` is pure math with no I/O: it computes the warm-only target, floors the hold-until to a quarter-hour boundary, and runs the `decide()` lifecycle that respects any manual hold a human set and refuses to drift cooler. `ownhold.py` persists the controller's last-pushed hold to disk so that after a restart it can identify and clean up only its OWN expired hold, never touching a hold someone else placed — that is spec Safety #3 made concrete.
tour.languageLesson: Functional-core / imperative-shell: `holds.py` is deliberately pure (inputs in, decision out, no side effects), so `decide()` can be unit-tested exhaustively without a real thermostat. The messy I/O — network pushes, disk writes — is pushed out to the loop and `ownhold.py`.

tour.title: The Thermostat Seam
tour.description: This is how a decision reaches real hardware. `device.py` is a thin facade exposing a synchronous snapshot/push/release interface to the loop, with exactly one network refresh per snapshot. Behind it, `tcc_client.py` is the Honeywell Total Connect Comfort adapter (backed by aiosomecomfort) that fills the ThermostatClient seam left when the old Control4 client was demolished. Timed holds — never Permanent — are the safety mechanism: if the controller dies, the thermostat reverts to its onboard schedule on its own.
tour.languageLesson: The 'seam' pattern: `device.py` wraps the async, network-bound `aiosomecomfort` client behind a small synchronous interface. The loop programs against the seam, not the vendor SDK, so the real cloud client can be swapped for a fake in tests and the Control4-to-Honeywell migration touched only one file.

tour.title: Telemetry Out
tour.description: Every tick leaves a record so the experiment is auditable. `telemetry.py` writes four streams through the whitelisted influx_adapter seam: hvac.actions rows (what was pushed), hvac.price_overlay tier transitions, hvac.arm_mode liveness rows, and decision-trace JSON lines that reconstruct exactly why the controller made each call. The arm_mode row is doubly important — it is the liveness beacon the Step 10 watchdog listens for.

tour.title: Safety Out-of-Band: The Watchdog
tour.description: Safety is device-owned, but a stalled controller is still worth knowing about. `check.py` runs as a separate service and never touches the thermostat: it queries InfluxDB for a recent hvac.arm_mode row (the beacon from Step 9) within a threshold window, and if none is found, writes an hvac.heartbeat point flagging the controller as stalled. This out-of-band supervisor is how a silent death becomes a visible alert rather than a thermostat quietly stuck warm.

tour.title: How Data Arrives
tour.description: Step back to where the whole loop's input originates. `poller.py` in comed_poller is the source of the sole live control input: on a wall-clock-aligned loop it fetches ComEd's current-hour-average and latest 5-minute prices and writes them to InfluxDB — the same bucket Step 5's pricing.py later reads fresh-strict. This is the pattern every ingest service in the stack follows: poll an external source, normalize, write to Influx, and let downstream consumers pull.

tour.title: Observed & Shipped
tour.description: The capstone: where controller state is watched and how code reaches the Pi. `telegram_notifier/app.py` runs a deduplicated alert loop over InfluxDB — poller silence, price spikes, feed-freshness, and the controller-down beacon from Step 10 — plus a daily summary. `cockpit/backend/app.py` is the FastAPI dashboard serving snapshot, day-ahead, and day-at-a-glance views over the same data. `docker-compose.yml` composes the whole fleet on Pi-lab, and `deploy.yml` closes the loop: merging to main is the deploy — a CI runner joins the tailnet, rsyncs the stack over Tailscale SSH, rebuilds, and smoke-tests that nothing crashed.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions YAML keys the whole deploy on `on: push` with a `paths:` filter (deploy/**), so only infrastructure changes ship. The runner is ephemeral — it joins the private tailnet as a short-lived node, does the work, and disappears — so no long-lived credential to Pi-lab sits in the cloud.
